rationale:
Evidence: iteration 4 is the best raced design (81.56). Its sensors sat at x = -0.06 to 0.06 with 0.016 m footprints at y = 0.05, with kp 7.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.4 and last_direction. It scored 135.7 on the oval (progress 0.33), 67.9 on the s-bend (progress 0.17) and 41.1 on the slalom (progress 0.10). Every one of 60 trials ended off track. Max error stayed at 0.063 m, just above the 0.06 m limit, and each run had about one line loss.

Accepted from the round-1 critique: (a) I drop the draft's 7-sensor array and y = 0.08 row. Its 'overlapping coverage' claim was false, and it changed several things at once. (b) I keep kd at 0.3. Iterations 1 and 2 showed that raising kd did not reduce steering_oscillation, so the draft's kd 1.5 is unsupported. (c) I keep kp 7.0, ki 0.1 and base_speed 1.4. Iteration 4 is the raced controller, and the critique is right that speed was never isolated, but cutting speed would reduce progress, which is worth 250 points directly. (d) I accept the point that the outer-reach argument must use the engagement figure. A sensor at x = 0.06 begins to see tape at about 0.04 m offset, and x = 0.08 would engage only at about 0.06 m, which is too late. So I keep x = ±0.06.

Rejected: the draft's claim that offset/0.06 weighting keeps kp 'near its tested value' is not a reason to change anything, so I keep the iteration-4 weights.

Change (single variable): sensor row moved forward from y = 0.05 to y = 0.07, with everything else identical to iteration 4. Forward lookahead lets the steering loop react earlier at bends, where the excursions occur. Because only geometry changes, any shift in max_error, line_loss_events or progress can be attributed to this change.

Hypotheses on the development tracks: max_error falls below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend; line_loss_events are 1 or fewer per run; oval progress stays at or above 0.33. If steering_oscillation rises by more than 30 percent, the next test is y = 0.06 rather than a kd change. If max_error gets worse, revert to y = 0.05. The slalom remains the weakest track, and completion at base_speed 1.4 is still untested, so completion_time and progress are requested.
